summary: The Senate passed a Transparency in Frontier AI Act (Sen. Barry Finegold) inside its economic development bill in July 2026, with catastrophic-risk frameworks and independent audits; it is in conference with the House. Gov. Healey has asked for stronger frontier provisions and federal guardrails.

items.title: Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act (Senate economic development bill, S.3228 §164)
items.text: Requires large frontier developers to adopt catastrophic-risk frameworks, undergo annual third-party compliance audits and independent catastrophic-risk evaluations at least every 120 days, and face AG enforcement; awaiting House-Senate conference.

items.title: Healey asks conference committee to strengthen frontier-AI section
items.text: Healey sought independent evaluation and lower harm thresholds for frontier-model reporting.

items.title: 26-AG letter to Congress on frontier AI safety
items.text: The Massachusetts attorney general signed the letter urging Congress to adopt federal frontier-AI safety rules and to bar preemption of state AI laws.

profile.headline: Massachusetts is funding shared AI computing for its universities while its governor pushes AI safety rules and local veto power over data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Maura Healey launched the Massachusetts AI Hub in December 2024 with $100 million authorized. Her September 8, 2026 executive order bars state permits for data centers over 25 MW without a local community-benefits agreement and requires their own clean power. On September 19, 2026 she proposed independent third-party testing of AI models, saying "AI companies cannot be allowed to self-assess their own models."

A $31 million state grant (May 2025) funds an AI computing cluster of several hundred NVIDIA GPUs at the MGHPCC in Holyoke, run on hydropower; Cambridge Computer was picked to build it in December 2025. Matching money is expected to bring the total above $120 million by 2030.

Everett's planning board voted on April 6, 2026 to cap data centers at 5 MW. Lowell residents sued in April 2026 over a Markley Group site's diesel generators. A ballot petition filed in August 2026 would require two-thirds voter approval for new data centers, and a Boston city councilor proposed a citywide ban in September 2026.
Boston University, Harvard, MIT, Northeastern, UMass and Yale are matching the state's $31 million for the shared Holyoke AI compute cluster.

Sen. Ed Markey released a draft Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act on July 13, 2026, requiring a federal certificate before construction, and reintroduced the AI Environmental Impacts Act with Rep. Don Beyer. Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Sen. Josh Hawley asked the Energy Information Administration to collect data-center energy data.
